title: Confidence is not evidence.
text: A confident answer can still be wrong. How can a learner see the difference between remembering a result and understanding an idea?

title: Make understanding visible.
text: Meet Gezhi: a learning workspace that connects your resources, your explanations, and evidence of your understanding.

title: One workspace. Your resources.
text: Start with a local library. Read your notes, follow their links, and keep your study materials together.

title: An AI that creates useful files.
text: Here, I ask the configured AI to create a Markdown study guide. This is a real request inside the software. The assistant writes a file into the demonstration library, including a worked example, a comparison table, and a self-check. Its output remains something I can inspect, edit, and question.

title: From a response to a study guide.
text: The new Markdown file appears in the library. I open it in Gezhi, where headings, tables and linked notes become a readable study guide.

title: Read the PDF. Stay in context.
text: The same guide is exported as a real PDF. Gezhi opens it inside the workspace, with page controls and zoom.

title: Word documents belong here too.
text: And the Word document opens here too. Markdown, PDF and Word materials can sit alongside the learning tools, without breaking the study flow.

title: You become the teacher.
text: Now I explain vertex form in my own words. My explanation contains a deliberate mistake: I call the vertex a minimum even when the curve opens downward. The real AI feedback identifies that condition and asks follow-up questions. The student still does the explaining; the AI helps expose the gaps. Typed explanations complement the voice input.

title: Commit confidence before feedback.
text: Before seeing feedback, I commit an answer and my confidence. This answer is wrong, although I marked it confident. Gezhi records that mismatch. A correct choice and a confident belief are different pieces of evidence.

title: Find the first broken step.
text: In Error Detective, a plausible solution hides a missing condition. Dividing by x loses the solution x equals zero. I identify the first incorrect step, select the repair, and explain why. The choice is checked; my written reasoning is saved separately.

title: Every judgment needs a trace.
text: The evidence map connects concepts to actual attempts. Select a node to inspect answers, confidence, and assistance. A confident error becomes a possible misconception, not a permanent label. Prerequisite arrows and associated concepts are distinguished. Note links have their own relationship graph.

title: Same idea. New conditions.
text: Understanding should travel beyond the first question. The transfer sequence moves from reading a vertex, to changing the sign of the coefficient, to locating the highest point of a fountain model. Each stage needs an answer and an explanation. Hints remain visible in the record, and later stages unlock after a pass.

title: Predict. Test. Explain.
text: In the concept workbench, change one condition and investigate. Adjusting a function parameter immediately changes its graph. The next step is to commit a numerical prediction and explain the relation behind it.

title: Turn equations into motion.
text: For force and motion, I predict acceleration from net force and mass. Then I run the three-second experiment. The animation and numerical result use the same simplified physical model, with its assumptions shown on screen.

title: Theory meets a fluctuating sample.
text: The probability experiment compares a theoretical chance with simulated random sampling. Repeated samples fluctuate. More data does not guarantee that every new sample moves closer to theory. Learners can save what they observe and explain.

title: A working prototype. Honest limits.
text: This demonstration uses original exercises in a simulated learning session. Engineering checks cover the learning flow and document readers; they are not evidence of improved student outcomes. Notes and records stay local. Selected content goes to the configured AI service, and AI feedback still needs review.

title: Read. Explain. Test. Transfer.
text: Gezhi turns study resources into a cycle of explanation, testing and discovery. Make understanding visible, one piece of evidence at a time.
